page: Amazon Web Services x8g.48xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 192 dedicated physical cores powered by the 64-bit ARM architecture AWS Neoverse-V2 processor running at 2.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 3072.0 GB of system memory, providing a high resource density of 16.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark data highlights top-tier multi-core capabilities and memory performance. The instance achieves top-tier results in multi-core CPU stress tests, multi-threaded decompression, and software compilation. Its memory subsystem delivers top-tier read and write bandwidth, which correlates with exceptional performance in database operations and Redis SET operations, where it processes hundreds of millions of operations per second. However, single-core performance and low-parameter LLM prompt processing are relatively average or weak, indicating that workloads must be highly parallelized to leverage the hardware fully.

Given the high memory-to-core ratio and the use of custom ARM-based Graviton silicon, the x8g.48xlarge offers high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound, highly parallel enterprise workloads. The absence of local storage and GPUs makes it less suitable for local-disk-heavy databases or hardware-accelerated machine learning training. It is best suited for large-scale in-memory databases, caching layers, big data analytics, and high-throughput web serving.
